newsitem.title: FRANCE: Up to French govt to negotiate on EMU pact-Chirac.
newsitem.headline: Up to French govt to negotiate on EMU pact-Chirac.

text.p: President Jacques Chirac believes it is up to the French government to negotiate on the EU "stability pact" but thinks its demands are justified, his spokeswoman said on Thursday.
"It is up to the government to conduct the talks. The President does not want to substitute for the government," spokeswoman Catherine Colonna told a news conference.
Asked whether the conservative Chirac backed the demands of the new Socialist-led government, Colonna said, "They seem justified to him."
The government has said it wants a greater focus on jobs and coordination of economic policies alongside the stability pact which limits budget deficits under monetary union.

Colonna said Chirac would meet Prime Minister Lionel Jospin for talks in between a Franco-German summit in Poitiers, western France on Friday and a European Union summit in Amsterdam on Monday. She gave no specific day or time. Jospin and Chirac will attend both summits.
The Franco-German summit was important, she said, but decisions had to be made by all 15 EU members. "It is a stage which I would describe as important. But you need 15 for an agreement," she said.
